newsitem.title: UK: BAA proposes new London-Heathrow rail link.
newsitem.headline: BAA proposes new London-Heathrow rail link.

text.p: British airports group BAA Plc said on Monday it was pressing ahead with proposals to operate a second rail link to Heathrow airport from central London, to complement its new Heathrow Express service due to open in 1998.

BAA said it hoped to get the go-ahead in the new year to run a new service from St Pancras station which would make use of the tunnels and stations it was building at the airport for the 400 million stg Heathrow Express line from Paddington station.

BAA said it would now be following up discussions held with interested parties, including regulator the Office of Passenger Rail Franchising, railway infrastructure operator Railtrack and the London & Continental Railways consortium which owns St Pancras as the chosen hub for its planned new fast railway for its Eurostar trains through the Channel Tunnel.
"The company would like to conclude these negotiations in the new year to enable it to place the order for new rolling stock," BAA said in a statement.

"The St Pancras service will be made possible by a private finance investment by BAA in rolling stock and infrastrucuture improvements at Heathrow and a major investment by Railtrack to fund the electrification and renewal of a lightly-used non-passenger line betweeen the Great Western Mainline and Midland Mainline at Cricklewood (in north London)," it said.
BAA is fighting to win planning approval to build a fifth passenger terminal at Heathrow designed to gradually boost capacity by 50 percent to 80 million passengers a year by 2016.

But the airport only has the one London Underground rail link into central London, and objectors say without better public transport the expansion will lead to ever bigger and more congested roads in the area.
BAA in turn has pledged to find ways of developing more rail and other public transport services to the airport.

"BAA concluded that investing in and operating the St Pancras service itself was the best way to maximise the use of public transport to and from Heathrow until a decision on whether Terminal Five should be built," it said on Monday.

"The new stopping service would also help to increase the number of Heathrow staff travelling to and from work by public transport. Over 50,0000 people work at the airport and many have no alternative but to drive to work."
